content.value_statement: TypeScript projects often drift into weak types, duplicated schemas, and fragile state models. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward safer TypeScript patterns.
actual_capabilities: Recommends discriminated unions for mutually exclusive request states.
Shows branded types for separating domain identifiers.
Promotes const assertions for keeping arrays and literal unions aligned.
Uses exhaustive switch checks with never for compile-time coverage.
Guides Zod schemas, safeParse, transforms, and inferred types.
Suggests type-fest utilities for advanced type helpers.
limitations: Does not inspect project files unless the host agent reads them.
Does not replace TypeScript compiler checks, linters, or tests.
Covers TypeScript language patterns, not React component architecture.
Offers examples, but users must adapt them to local conventions.

use_cases.title: Model application state safely
use_cases.description: A frontend engineer can replace boolean flags with discriminated unions and exhaustive checks.

use_cases.title: Validate API boundaries
use_cases.description: A backend developer can pair Zod schemas with inferred types for request and response data.

use_cases.title: Review shared TypeScript libraries
use_cases.description: A technical lead can standardize branded types, const assertions, and utility types across packages.

prompt_templates.title: Find unsafe states
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my TypeScript type definitions and suggest safer alternatives using this skill. Focus on illegal states and simple explanations.

prompt_templates.title: Improve validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this input handling flow. Recommend Zod schemas, safe parsing, transforms, and inferred types where they fit.

prompt_templates.title: Strengthen domain types
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these domain identifiers and data models. Suggest branded types, const assertions, and exhaustive checks for stronger guarantees.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TypeScript best-practices migration plan for this codebase. Prioritize state modeling, validation boundaries, and reusable utility types.

output_examples.input: A request state type uses loading, data, and error fields together.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends separate idle, loading, success, and error variants to prevent impossible state combinations.

output_examples.input: A form handler parses untrusted user input before saving it.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests a Zod schema, safe parsing, normalized fields, and clear validation errors.

output_examples.input: User identifiers and order identifiers are both plain strings.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends branded domain identifiers so different string IDs are not mixed accidentally.

best_practices: Use discriminated unions when states are mutually exclusive.
Validate external data at trust boundaries and infer types from schemas.
Add exhaustive checks when branching over literal unions.
anti_patterns: Representing state with independent booleans that can conflict.
Duplicating runtime schemas and TypeScript types by hand.
Using plain strings for domain identifiers that should not mix.

faq.question: What files does this skill support?
faq.answer: It is intended for TypeScript, JavaScript, TSX, JSX, and tsconfig-related work.

faq.question: Does it replace a TypeScript compiler?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, while the compiler, linter, and tests verify the code.

faq.question: Can it help with runtime validation?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends Zod schemas, safe parsing, transforms, and inferred TypeScript types.

faq.question: Does it cover React best practices?
faq.answer: Only TypeScript fundamentals. The skill recommends pairing it with a React-specific skill for component work.

faq.question: Is type-fest required?
faq.answer: No. The skill presents type-fest as an optional source of advanced utility types.

faq.question: Which agents can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
